findings.checklist_item: Reconcile the assignee overlay shape: the mutation `fields` dict carries assignee as a bare resolved accountId string, but the baseline's assignee_identity is derived (via InboundMapper._identity_of) from a raw Jira user DICT — specify how the overlay reconstructs a dict-shaped assignee (or an assignee_identity) so re-projection does not yield an empty identity, or explicitly exclude assignee from the overlay with a stated reason.
evidence: normalize_baseline_value (inbound_fields.py:148-154) only unwraps priority/status dicts and passes other values through unchanged, so set_baseline stores the assignee value verbatim.
The baseline is re-projected via InboundMapper.jira_fields_to_canonical, which for assignee computes out['assignee_identity']=_identity_of(jira_fields.get('assignee')) (inbound_fields.py:237).
_identity_of (inbound_fields.py:186-192) returns a real identity ONLY for a dict input (raw Jira user object); a bare string returns {display:None,email:None,account_id:None}.
map_fields_to_remote (adapters/jira_family/outbound_mapper.py:85-88) passes assignee through as resolve_assignee's output — a bare accountId string, NOT a Jira user dict.

_suppressed_by_inbound for assignee reads baseline.get('assignee') AND baseline.get('assignee_identity') via _assignee_matches (outbound_field_diff.py:329-332, 402-404), so a wrong/empty identity in the overlaid baseline breaks assignee arbitration.
findings.finding: The plan asserts the vendor-shaped mutation `fields` dict is exactly the shape set_baseline/normalize_baseline_value consume with no new mapping layer, but this is false for the assignee field, so overlaying assignee will corrupt its baseline identity projection.
findings.location: Approach section — 'The mutation fields dict is already vendor-shaped... which is exactly the shape peer_state.set_baseline / normalize_baseline_value consume — so the overlay needs no new mapping layer'; and 'Applied to all five _INBOUND_MIRRORED_FIELDS'
scenarios: A pass pushes an assignee change outbound; the overlay writes a bare accountId string as baseline['assignee']; the next pass re-projects assignee_identity as all-None, so _assignee_matches mis-fires and the assignee ABA guard is wrong.
findings.suggested_fix: For the assignee field, overlay the raw Jira user object rebar just pushed (or synthesize {accountId: <value>} so _identity_of recovers account_id) instead of the bare resolved string; alternatively write assignee_identity directly into the baseline. State this per-field shape handling explicitly rather than the blanket 'no new mapping layer' claim.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State whether the soft-fail / baseline-not-advanced path emits an operator-visible signal (log/metric), or record a rationale for why continued silence is acceptable given the conservative all-or-nothing design.
evidence: The plan itself diagnoses the current class as 'Silent: the pass exits 0 and nothing is logged as a conflict.'
The conservative design ('any raise ... records NOTHING, so the baseline can only ever lag') means a soft-failed field stays divergent across passes with no stated log/metric.
No log/metric/trace is described for the baseline-overlay or the soft-fail-skip path.
findings.finding: The plan's fix removes the silent clobber but adds no new instrumentation for the soft-fail non-advance case, where a mutation fails, the baseline is deliberately NOT advanced, and local/remote remain divergent with nothing surfaced to operators.
findings.location: Approach steps 1-5 and 'Blast radius' ('Silent: the pass exits 0 and nothing is logged as a conflict')
scenarios: A status transition soft-fails (400 illegal-transition comment-fallback); baseline is not advanced; the field stays out of sync silently across subsequent passes with no operator-visible signal.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a debug/info log line at the soft-fail arm (or where merge_baseline skips a field) naming the local_id and field left unadvanced, so a persistently-divergent field is discoverable in pass logs.
